Subject: Redwood vendor onboarding: procurement + data governance checkpoint

Ethan —

Quick intro from procurement at Redwood — I own vendor setup and PO flow. We're starting the onboarding checklist for DataSafe Solutions and need a few items to complete our procurement and privacy intake:

1) DPA: do you have a standard Data Processing Agreement you provide to customers? If so, please attach the latest PDF and indicate whether you accept counterparty edits or require your baseline.

2) Subprocessors: a current list of subprocessors (name, purpose, country, whether they have access to customer plaintext).

3) Data retention: default retention periods for customer-generated content, logs, and backups, and whether customers can request custom retention terms.

4) PO & billing: do you require a PO to be raised before going live? Standard payment terms (Net30/Net45), invoice remit details, and any minimum contract value.

5) Security artifacts: SOC 2 report, penetration test summary, or a link to an attestation. We can accept redacted copies if needed.

6) Onboarding form: we have a short vendor intake form (I can send) — any preferences for format (PDF, online form)?

If you can send the DPA + subprocessors + SOC2 by EOD Tue (13 Apr), that should keep us on schedule to issue a PO the following week. I can coordinate DocuSign if you prefer.

Thanks — concise answers are fine; we can follow up on items that need negotiation.

Karthik Iyer
Vendor Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear list. Answers below and I've attached the items you asked for.

1) DPA: attached (datasafe_dpa_v1.pdf). We typically start with our standard DPA but are open to limited, mutual edits on customer-specific clauses (data location, audit rights). We prefer DocuSign for signature.

2) Subprocessors: attached CSV (datasafe_subprocessors_20260413.csv) — includes name, purpose, country, and whether they ever handle decrypted content. Short summary: core cloud infra (AWS us-west-2) — no plaintext access; analytics vendor has hashed/aggregated data only.

3) Data retention: default retention policies: customer content (90 days by default, configurable), logs/telemetry (365 days), backups (encrypted, retained 180 days). We support customer-specific retention via contract; some customers request 30/90/365 splits depending on regulatory needs.

4) PO & billing: yes, we accept POs. Standard terms: Net30. Invoice remit: accounting@datasafe.com. Minimum contract value: none for standard SaaS; bespoke engagements may have a minimum.

5) Security artifacts: attached redacted SOC 2 (datasafe_soc2_redacted_2025.pdf). We can provide a SOC 2 letter under NDA if required.

6) Onboarding form: PDF or online is fine. If you send your intake form, I'll get our onboarding lead to fill it out.

DocuSign: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234-efgh-5678

Attachments: datasafe_dpa_v1.pdf (PDF, 92KB), datasafe_subprocessors_20260413.csv (CSV, 6KB), datasafe_soc2_redacted_2025.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Let me know if you want a quick 20-minute sync to walk through.

—Ethan Brooks

Thanks, Ethan — helpful. A few clarifying/follow-up items from Redwood legal/procurement:

- Retention: when you say "customer content (90 days by default, configurable)", can you confirm whether the 90 days applies to generated model outputs, logs that contain customer queries, or both? We need explicit separation for contract language.

- Subprocessor access: your note says core infra has "no plaintext access" and analytics has "hashed/aggregated" — can you confirm if any subprocessors have live access to unredacted customer content (e.g., for troubleshooting)? If so, please list which subprocessors and under what circumstances.

- DPA edits: Laura (cc'd) from legal will drive any redlines. Is your team open to a single redline cycle (mutual edits plus signature), or do you require using your baseline without changes?

- SOC 2: Laura will review the redacted report. If we need an unredacted version or management letter under NDA, we'll request it.

Finally, we'll need an invoice remit and a PO contact person for procurement to include in our purchase order.

If you can reply with the two clarifications above and indicate DocuSign readiness, we can move to PO issuance.

Karthik

Karthik / Laura / Monica —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers below; happy to expand.

- Retention clarification: the 90-day default applies only to customer-generated content (e.g., files, user prompts, model outputs). Logs that capture telemetry and request metadata are retained 365 days. Backups are encrypted and retained for 180 days. We can put language in the DPA to explicitly separate "Customer Content" and "Operational Logs" retention windows.

- Subprocessor access: none of our analytics providers or third parties have access to unredacted customer content under normal operations. The only scenario where a subprocessors could access plaintext is if a customer explicitly opts into a support session where they share logs or data — in that case access is performed by a named support vendor under a scoped NDAs and logged in our internal ticketing system. I've updated the subprocessors CSV to include an "access_scope" column and re-attached a marked-up DPA that calls this out.

- DPA edits: we are open to a single mutual redline cycle. We've attached datasafe_dpa_markedup_20260414.pdf with the suggested clarifying clause for retention and subprocessor access. Once agreed we can route via DocuSign.

- PO contact: please route POs to orders@datasafe.com. For billing inquiries: accounting@datasafe.com.

Attachments: datasafe_dpa_markedup_20260414.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

If Laura wants to schedule a quick 20-minute call to go over the DPA language, I'm available Tue afternoon (PST).

Best,
Ethan
